items.entity: Single unit point load for the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says the load is 'randomly sampled from an element along the boundary of the domain'. The text never gives the edge or element used for this sample. The Fig. 5 caption mentions only the ground-truth, output and difference images and does not say the load is marked. At best the position could be guessed from the ground-truth topology image.
readings: Top edge, element k (k=0..63): load at x=(k+0.5)/64 of the width
Bottom edge, element k: load at x=(k+0.5)/64 of the width
Left edge, element k: load at y=(k+0.5)/64 of the height
Right edge, element k: load at y=(k+0.5)/64 of the height

items.entity: How the element-based load is applied to FE nodes
items.description: Sec. 4.1 samples the load at a boundary element, and Eq. 24 stores it as an element load vector F_e. Supports, however, are defined on nodes, and FE forces act on nodes. The text does not say which node(s) carry the unit force, or which edge is used for a corner element.
readings: Full unit force at one node of the element's outer edge (position k/64)
Full unit force at the other outer-edge node (position (k+1)/64)
Split equally between the two outer-edge nodes (uniform traction over one element edge)
Split equally among all four element nodes
Corner element: force applied at the corner node

items.entity: Load angle for the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the direction is 'sampled from an angle of 0 to 360° from 6 evenly distributed angles'. The angle used for this sample is not in the text, and the caption does not say it is drawn in Fig. 5.
readings: 72°, 144°, 216° or 288° (if the angles are spaced 72° apart)
30°, 90°, 150°, 210°, 270° or 330° (offset grid, or a sample rotated 90° during augmentation)

items.entity: Set of 6 'evenly distributed' admissible angles
items.description: In Sec. 4.1, 'from an angle of 0 to 360° from 6 evenly distributed angles' can be read as 60° steps with 360° excluded, or as linspace(0,360,6) (72° steps, with 0°≡360°, giving only 5 distinct directions). Sec. 4.1 also says the data were augmented by rotation and mirroring, which can move the displayed sample's angle outside the original set.
readings: Original set enlarged by 90° rotations and mirroring (e.g., all multiples of 30°)

items.entity: Reference axis and sense of the load angle; mapping from image to FE axes
items.description: The text does not say which axis the angle is measured from, in which direction, or how the image rows and columns in Figs. 1 and 5 map to FE x/y (y up or y down in image indexing). If this is misread, the load is mirrored relative to the supports.
readings: Counter-clockwise from +x, with y pointing up (Cartesian)
From +x with y pointing down (image row index), i.e., clockwise as displayed

items.entity: Fixed supports (number and identity) for the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says each sample has 1–4 boundary conditions chosen from 16 candidates: 4 corner nodes, 4 edge-midpoint nodes and 8 corner-to-midpoint half-edge node sets, all fixed in x and y. The number and choice for this sample are not in the text, and the caption does not say supports are drawn.
readings: One half-edge node set clamped (e.g., left edge, y in [0, 0.5])
One whole edge clamped (both half-edge sets, e.g., entire left edge)
Corner node(s) plus edge-midpoint node(s) pinned (e.g., (0,0) and (1,0.5))
Any other combination of 1–4 of the 16 candidates

items.entity: Extent of the half-edge (corner-to-midpoint) node sets
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'The sets of nodes between corners and midpoints' but does not say whether the end nodes (the corner node and the midpoint node 32 of 0..64) belong to the set.
readings: Both end nodes excluded (31 interior nodes)

items.entity: Configurations with a single point support
items.description: Sec. 4.1 allows a single boundary condition and lists single node points as candidates. One node fixed in x and y still lets the body rotate freely, so K is singular. This contradicts Sec. 2.1, which says E_min keeps the equilibrium problem 'well defined for any valid structure'. The text does not say how such samples were handled.
readings: The sample has at least 2 point supports or at least 1 half-edge set (well-posed; nothing to add)
Single pinned node plus an unstated extra restraint (e.g., a roller) to stop rotation
Samples with a single point support were discarded
Solver regularization (e.g., weak springs) used to make K non-singular

items.entity: Target volume fraction f for the Fig. 5 row-1 sample
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the range 'from 30% to 50%' and does not say whether sampling is continuous or discrete. The value for this sample is not stated. It could only be estimated from the solid-pixel fraction of the binarized ground-truth image, which may differ from f after Heaviside thresholding.
readings: Solid-pixel fraction measured from the ground-truth image

items.entity: Young's modulus E0 used in the optimization
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives a unit elastic modulus for the pre-processing FEA (stress and strain-energy fields on the initial domain). The text does not separately state the E0 used by the optimizer that produced the ground truth.

items.entity: 2D stress state and Poisson's ratio in the optimization
items.description: The text never says whether plane stress or plane strain is used. ν = 0.3 is stated only for the pre-processing FEA (Sec. 4.1). Plane strain with ν = 0.3 behaves like plane stress with ν ≈ 0.43.
readings: Plane stress with a different ν in the optimizer

items.entity: Void stiffness E_min (Eq. 5)
items.description: Eq. 5 and the text after it introduce E_min but give no value.

items.entity: SIMP penalty p
items.description: Sec. 2.1 says p is 'commonly set to 3' but does not confirm the value used for the dataset. Sec. 1 mentions continuation schemes in general without saying whether one was used.

items.entity: Density or sensitivity filter type and radius
items.description: No density or sensitivity filter type or radius is given anywhere. Sec. 4.1 mentions only a Heaviside filter.
readings: No density or sensitivity filter (Heaviside only)

items.entity: Heaviside filter / binarization of the ground truth
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'with a Heaviside filter to ensure binary output images'. It does not say whether this is a projection inside the optimization or a threshold applied after convergence. β, η, any continuation, and whether the volume constraint uses the projected densities are all unstated.
readings: Threshold at ρ = 0.5 applied after convergence
Volume-preserving threshold after convergence (the f·4096 densest elements set solid)
Heaviside projection during optimization, η = 0.5, β continuation (e.g., doubling from 1 to 64)
Heaviside projection during optimization with fixed β (e.g., 8–16)

items.entity: Optimization method and update scheme used for the ground truth
items.description: Sec. 2.1 describes SIMP with 'an optimization algorithm such as MMA'. Sec. 4.1 refers only to 'the topology optimization method'. The method actually used and its parameters (move limits, asymptote settings) are not given.
readings: SIMP + MMA with standard Svanberg settings
SIMP + GCMMA or another gradient-based optimizer

items.entity: Stopping criterion
items.description: Sec. 2.1 (Eq. 7) allows either a relative-compliance tolerance ε or 'iteration count limits', but gives neither ε nor an iteration limit.

items.entity: Initial density field
items.description: No starting design is given. Sec. 1 itself notes that iterative schemes are sensitive to the initial guess.

items.entity: Finite-element type on the 64×64 grid
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only '64×64 domain of square elements'. The element formulation and integration rule are not stated.
readings: Q4 with incompatible modes or reduced integration

items.entity: Physical element size and out-of-plane thickness
items.description: Only the element counts (64×64) are given (Sec. 4.1); physical dimensions and thickness are not. For square 2D elements under nodal loads, compliance does not depend on element side length, and it scales as 1/t with thickness t.

items.entity: Passive (fixed solid or void) elements
items.description: No passive regions are mentioned. The load-discrepancy metric (Sec. 4.3, Eq. 24) expects material at the loaded element, but the text does not say whether that element was forced solid in the ground-truth optimization.
readings: Loaded and supported elements forced solid
